subject: Model fit / evals follow-up: tool calling & structured output
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Hernandez <sofia@finbank.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-24T16:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap + next steps (model fit & evals)

Hi Sofia — thanks again for a great conversation today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can keep momentum: 

1) Priorities you called out:
- High-accuracy structured outputs for regulatory reporting (JSON schema compliance is mandatory)
- Low 95th%-ile latency for short prompts (customer-facing summaries)
- Cost predictability for monthly transaction volumes (~50M tokens/month)

2) Recommended initial model candidates from our catalog:
- redwood-3b-structured-v1 (FP16, good JSON schema adherence in our evals)
- open-llm-7b-quant (int8) — strong cost/latency tradeoff for bulk batch scoring
- redwood-13b-tooling (FP16 + tool-calling hooks) — if you need richer external API calls and complex function orchestration

3) Evals and artifacts attached: eval_results_summary.csv (overview), prompt_set_v2.jsonl (your anonymized examples + extra edge cases), redwood_benchmark_report.pdf (latency/%cost profiles). Links below as well.

4) Tool/function-calling notes we discussed:
- We validated JSON-schema enforcement with our structured output eval harness; see "schema-strict" mode results in the CSV (column: json_schema_fail_rate). Current failure mode for open-llm-7b-quant is mainly missing fields on deeply nested objects; retry logic (idempotent-safe) reduces visible failures to near-zero for small batches.
- For stateful function calling (payments lookups, KYC fetch), recommended pattern: separate small tool calls (fast RPC) from bulk generation; use the runtime's retry-on-timeout with idempotency token (we'll provide code samples).

5) Next steps (can we agree?):
- We (Redwood) will run a short benchmark on your production-like prompt set (using prompt_set_v2.jsonl) across the three model candidates and share a short prioritized recommendation by Tue 4/27.
- Sofia / FinBank: share any additional high-risk prompt examples (PII-heavy or edge case regulatory scenarios) and confirm who from Procurement we should loop in for T&C talks.
- Schedule a technical walkthrough next week to go through the eval results and integration approach.

If that aligns, I will kick off the run and send calendar invites for the walkthrough.

Thanks — Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0142
https://www.redwood.ai

Attachments referenced: eval_results_summary.csv, prompt_set_v2.jsonl, redwood_benchmark_report.pdf

From: Sofia Hernandez <sofia@finbank.com>

Subject: Re: Discovery recap + next steps (model fit & evals)

Hi Marissa — this is perfect, thanks for the clear recap. A few quick answers: 

- I'll add three more regulator-focused examples to the Drive folder by EOD today.
- Procurement contact is procurement@finbank.com (cc'd on the next message).
- For the walkthrough, Tue 4/27 at 10am PT works for our infra + risk pair.

Quick question on the JSON schema failures: what do you mean by "schema-strict" mode? Is that something our engineers need to implement or is it handled by Redwood's SDK/runtime?

Thanks, Sofia
Sofia Hernandez
Head of ML Integrations, FinBank
sofia@finbank.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Procurement <procurement@finbank.com>
Cc: Sofia Hernandez <sofia@finbank.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-28T08:05:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Discovery recap + next steps (model fit & evals)

Hi Procurement team — looping you in per Sofia's note. We're preparing a short benchmark and an initial technical recommendation for FinBank's regulatory reporting use case. High-level commercial ask up front: we will propose a 3-month pilot on a dedicated inference pool (predictable latency, isolated data) and a usage estimate for the pilot in the benchmark report.

For procurement: attached is a current Redwood pilot SOW template (link below) and the HubSpot deal is RDW-2027-0457 if you need a record. Can someone confirm contracting lead and any required PO/terms timing?

Technical note for your engineers (cc Rishi & Aditya): the "schema-strict" mode I referenced is part of our eval harness — it's an evaluation setting that enforces exact JSON schema conformance when scoring. In prod, you can: 
- Enable runtime output validation (SDK side) to reject non-conforming outputs before ingestion, and then either retry or call a maintenance function to repair/normalize; or
- Use the runtime's function-calling pattern where the model returns only a set of params and Redwood's runtime maps/validates them against the schema before returning to your application.

Rishi / Aditya — can you two prepare a 2-slide tech summary on the schema-strict mode and recommended retry policy (idempotency keys, max attempts, backoff) for Tue's walkthrough?

Thanks,
Marissa

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-30T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Discovery recap + next steps (model fit & evals)

Sounds good — I'll take the schema-strict slide and outline the runtime validation flow (validation hooks, fallback repair function, and integration points). Aditya, can you own the benchmark run config and include the quantized candidate (open-llm-7b-quant) with batch sizes 1, 8, 32 and measure json_schema_fail_rate + 95th%-ile latency?

I'll draft recommended retry policy: 3 attempts, exponential backoff starting at 150ms, idempotency token per logical request. I'll also include notes about when to prefer function-calling (for small, critical RPCs) vs. direct generation (for bulk summarization).

Rishi
Director, Applied ML — Redwood Inference
